name: sticky-cta-bar
title: Sticky CTA bar
description: A bar fixed to the bottom that appears once the hero has scrolled away, with the product, a price or promise and one action; it can be dismissed.
docs: Pass label, description, action and, when it should appear, showAfter: a number of pixels from the top, or the id of an element (usually the hero) that has to scroll out of view first. hideWhen is the id of an element, such as the footer or a sign-up form, that hides the bar for as long as any part of it is on screen. The bar watches both with IntersectionObserver, so there is no scroll handler. It slides in with a short transform that becomes a fade for people who prefer less motion, floats as a card from 640px and is a full-width strip on a phone, keeps clear of the safe area, and is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree whenever it is hidden. While it shows it adds room at the bottom of the page and a scroll padding, so it never covers the last lines or a focused field. dismissible adds a labelled close button, onDismiss is called, and storageKey remembers the choice for the browser session; closed from the keyboard, focus goes back to the element it came from. Inside a preview frame, a dialog or any pane that scrolls instead of the window, pass that element as scrollRoot (a ref): the bar is then positioned inside it rather than fixed to the screen.
